comment: Nice trail. We took the trail to see cataract falls. Really enjoyed the view and the well maintained trail. Our dog had a blast! Look out for bugs though! Parking is ample, just don’t forget to book online as you require a booking/barcode to open the gate.
Too many bugs for the first half of the trail
We got a great workout hiking to the falls. It’s not an easy trek but worth it. Not for small children. Plan up to 4 hours for that trek.
It was easy to find parking, there’s additional parking also. But not much of a view for that kind of hike we had to do.
Beautiful area in any season nice challenging Hills walk along the river. Definitely an excellent place to go.
At this time of year, the apple blossoms and the lilac trees are stunning. There was a lot of bird song to hear.

Well kept trail, moderately challenging 10km because of the variety of terrain - up and down. Good cardio work out for sure! The Cataract falls are really nice, and enjoyed the bridge too. Would recommend for sure!
Great trail, lots of big hills, rocks and roots. Wear good hiking shoes and lots of water.

Great trails with stunning views! Hike was steep at times and heavy incline. Cataract waterfall was okay, but there is no clear or close view of the falls (the trail was closed off at a certain point). The variety of scenery from rolling meadows, to tall forests to evergreens was beautiful. Would highly recommend.
The water is fast moving and high.  Conditions were great!
Great long trail! Great views
Beautiful river views.. waterfall and mix of flat and slopes
A nice loop in the park! Nothing strenuous, some uphill sections but easy moving. Nice views of the river and falls!
Harder than expected, but if your an avid hiker looking for a variety of diverse terrain it’s great park, wasn’t busy middle of the week. Will be returning without a doubt
Entry fee, bathrooms available, gradual elevation, and scenic views of a winding river.
Beautiful trail with some elevation. The river and the falls make it worth visiting.
Amazing view. Definitely very hilly!
Beautiful day. Trails are in good condition with only a few slightly muddy spots that are easily avoided. Washrooms at parking lot are open.
For early April, parts of the Bruce trail along the escarpment are covered in ice (even when 20 C outside). Use caution
Nice in the winter

It was a nice loops, some beautiful views of the river, I wouldn’t have included the waterfall, as it’s just a long walk to return to the same point crossed before, other than that conditions were good, keep in mind it’s tough because of the terrain type and elevation, but the best this in addition to the river views, it has lots of pine trees combined with other Ontario trees, most leaves have fallen though
One of my favourite parks in Ontario. Going in the fall during late October/November resembles a Tom Thompson painting with the how desolate the trail feels.

The forest is a bit gloomy with all the leaves down but the conditions were pretty good. The waterfall lookout is still terrible, but it does look like they're finally working on it based on what I saw. Trails are all well kept and immaculate on both the Bruce and trans-Canada side. People really need to pick up after their dogs though.
Definitely past autumn peak but still a beautiful hike
10 Credit Park Street, Belfountain, Caledon
The hike was nice, there are some climbs. So much litter on the trail!!! Very rude and inconsiderate to litter in nature. My friends started picking up trash along the way
Nice trail, not really much of a hike. The waterfall was a decent view, but the view was better if you went past the fence and down a bit . Nice fall colours, and very easy.

This is a truly multidimensional trail and has some very scenic views! The river is absolutely beautiful and the fall colours are amazing! The elevation is just right enough to make for some good cardio but not overwhelming. All in all comes just under 20K steps so one gets a good decent workout!

Some sections of the trail are challenging and quite enjoyable. The challenging ones thankfully tend to be the ones less traveled by the noisy obnoxious people that are just there for social media. No bugs, trail quite dusty in areas. Would recommend if you're in the area.
We really enjoyed it, beautiful fall colors and weather, great views and mixed terrain. Loved it
Great hike, amazing views. Not to hard in terms of elevation, although you do have to pay ~9$ for a parking permit. Overall amazing!
Trail was amazing and took you to all the viewpoints! All the viewing platforms were closed, but still able to see the falls and stream.
Beautiful hike, specially in September.  Main parking didn't let me book, so I drove to the far parking and ....
Trails are well groomed with lots of elevation in areas. Bring water. The washrooms are not very gross, so plan ahead.
I definitely recommend forks of  Credit provincial Park

Started by taking the trail to the right at the start,  lots of flat areas and a few inclines at the beginning of the trail. Large set of stairs to walk up. End of the trail had a lot of inclines but manageable. Beautiful views, great conditions.
Book and pay for parking
There are washrooms
your legs will be on fire but it’s a great trail
This trail always a treat. A good workout with all the ups and downs  but also quiet and peaceful.

This is a very heavy incline hike if you head in the direction of the waterfall first! Beware of this! Can be pretty buggy in spots, not well maintained in other spots, but most of it is okay! The waterfall is the best part! You can easily hop the fence and head towards the base, getting back up is tricky, but doable. UGH but PLEASE take your garbage with you!
Fairly buggy still, be prepared for that
First ever hike, great introduction to the hobby.
One frog, okay but not very interesting.
Nice easy trail. Mostly flat except for two parts with elevation. People need to stop littering and clean up after themselves!
Website says park opens at 8am, but I got here at 5:30 and the gate was open, I was only one here so I cleared all the spider webs for the next group of hikers!
Lovely trial lots of different type of terrain!

The meadows, river and waterfalls are absolutely beautiful and definitely worth the visit. 

I recommend buying a parking pass/day pass before you reach the entrance because there is limited internet service there 

Overall really cool park and trails!
Beautiful hike for a warm day. Gorgeous scenery
Very well maintained and clean, Bruce Trail portion not busy at all considering a long weekend.

Have to reserve a day pass online before coming, and was asked by a warden upon entering. But plenty of parking available, well-marked and maintained trails. The view of the waterfall might be better with less foliage, but there was another lovely pond to stop at and several nice spots along the Credit River. Elevation changes were very manageable for my group and I really enjoyed walking through the open meadows with lots of fragrant apple trees in blossom. I think I will come again and try a trail run another day as the footing is quite forgiving, even if the elevation might be a challenge!
Well maintained, easy parking. Always save your parking pass as a photo because service could be spotty.
Nice trail
Great trail with excellent elevations along the hike

Good hiking trail, but this is NOT bicycle friendly. 

Dangerous speeds and turns and huge fall-offs to the side.

Do not reccomend for mountain biking, for anyone below advanced/expert.
no bugs at all. lots of elevation. one of the best trails in Ontario.
Great area, challenging heels, beautiful waterfall fast flowing river definitely recommended

This park has some awesome trails for all kinds of hikers. We mixed it up on our hike and got a taste of everything—but if you’re short on time, there are lots of connections to other trails so you can make it as long or as short as you like.

You’ll find a bit of the Bruce Trail, peaceful meadows, shady cedar and pine forests, a big waterfall, a beautiful river, some fun ups and downs, bridges… it really has a little bit of everything. You can take it at your own pace—fast, slow, or somewhere in between. It’s kind of like a choose-your-own-adventure hike!

Quick heads up: the mid-trail washrooms were closed when we went, so plan accordingly!

Whether you’re a seasoned hiker or just starting out, this one’s definitely worth checking out. Hope you get a chance to explore it!

The trail was mostly dry, only some short parts where it was a bit muddy or there were some tiny snow patches left. The small portion of the trail next to the waterfall was still closed (as of April 13), but very walkable (just don't tell anyone, shhhh!). Overall it was a well maintained trail. The walk is easy, almost no hill, pretty shaded except for the stretch near the parking lot. The view was okay, the part next to the river is cute, but the waterfall is underwhelming.
Great trail. The route that we took was a little challenging so recommend packing some healthy snack and water. A good hiking shoe is mandatory.
Bathrooms still closed for winter, parts of trail near river flooded and muddy
Beautiful trail and perfect 2hour loop

Kinda boring to be honest. The waterfall is underwhelming (Tew falls 10x better). Lots of little bridges - kinda cool. Pretty much the rest is just a meandering forest trail.  Gate reservation didnt work - late night.. Oops wrong day. But, eventually found a place to park right off Mississauga Rd. Now the bad news. Loop trail to waterfall lookout closed. Construction? And lots of slippery wet ice and thick mushy snow.

LOTS of snow still. Not just in the shady areas. I think there must’ve been some good snow drifts so it’s knee deep in some sections. Very muddy as well. Hopefully it melts fast!! Only saw about 8 other people for the 2 hours I hiked and saw some wildlife .
Packed snow trail, narrow, no mud yet.
What a wonderful trail! I highly recommend it.
4 inches of snow overnight  lots of elevation gain. One of the better workout hikes around here.
Beautiful

Forks of the Credit, always a good hike. Keep low expectations of the falls view, looks like there is still some trail construction, it's mostly obscured by trees. Opt instead for river side Dominion. Lots of elevation changes makes for a quick heart rate and sweet views. Not icy at the moment, but  strap on the crampons for easier passage.  Book your timed parking permit in advance on Ontario Parks website. Happy hiking!
Nice trails but facilities are not easily accessible
Slippery in sections at the beginning, but otherwise very beautiful. We had the park to ourselves on a Monday in November.

This trail is well marked and easy to follow. There are quite a few hills but definitely worth it. The hike was very peaceful, and scenic hike. We enjoyed it with our dog. Definitely book your reservation before hand or you’ll have to waste time upon arrival booking it online.

Great variety of trails including the Bruce Trail, which is narrow at times but beautiful scenery. Some stairs involved in the middle of a trail with higher and lower elevations. Downloading the free All Trails maps were a helpful guide.

Make sure to buy your parking pass online first! The trail itself is quite nice, built into the valley. There's quite a lot of people on the path to the falls but the side paths were much quieter. Overall a pretty decent hike close to the GTA!

I was there on a Monday early afternoon  and it was pretty quiet, I tried to get in the day before (Sunday) and it was completely full and booked for the day. 
It was a great hike but I couldn’t do the entire loop as it seemed to be closed off.  The trail to the falls was nice and there was lots of beautiful scenery. 
The only downside,  was that you have to prebook and prepay which loses in spontaneity
Nice trail, well indicated. Lots of views and open spaces!

We had a great time hiking on this trail! The path was well-maintained, with beautiful views along the way. The difficulty was moderate, making it an enjoyable way to explore the park without being too strenuous. Highly recommend for anyone looking to spend a nice day outdoors!

Need a reservation to get in, that never used to be the case. Used to love coming here but sucks that you can’t get in anymore.

Book your spot in advance

Easy hike for the most part…some hilly and steep inclines and downhills…Wearing hiking boots or shoes would be advisable on the hilly portions to avoid slipping on stones covered with leaves and loose gravel..otherwise a nice moderate hike !!
Moderate difficulty with a few strenuous climbs. Very well maintained and marked. Nice variety of landscapes and views.
Bring snacks,  plenty of nice places to have a break
Beautiful trail reminder to register it’s a paid trail enjoy!

Great hike! Mostly dirt/roots/rock pathway, between a mix of forest & meadows. Some parts of the trail are fairly easy and a nice trail walk, but there are hills, and they’re steep and long, making this, overall, a more moderately-difficult hike …but lovely and worth it!
Great trial

Great views throughout! Would recommend starting the loop clockwise to leave the better views for later. Trail is clearly marked and easy to follow, there are a few turns marked on the map that lead into super overgrown areas, but if you follow the marked trails you should be able to avoid them without missing out on anything. Bugs are not too bad this time of the year but would still recommend bug spray!
Paid. A cold rainy day hike with lovely views.
leg workout

Amazing trail loop, when you get to the closed section by the falls go up the steep hill and join the main trail rather than turning around for some extra challenge. Some spots are overgrown but clean, maintained trails for the most part. Nice staircase by the falls too.
A good trail with some hilly climbs and slopes. Moderate to difficult, I appreciated all the trail markers making it very easy to stay on the trail and know where I am
Moderately difficult trail with great site seeing!

There appears to be no valid parking at the location listed as the trailhead. The automatic gate for the paid lot at Forks of the Credit is located on McLaren Road (address: 17760 McLaren Rd, Caledon, ON).
Beautiful park, wonderful trail! Little buggy in places, but thankfully I remembered bug spray today.  Parts were overgrown, but not too terrible.  Lovely mix of up and down, meadows, woods, water.

nice trails, very brushy - wear long pants or high socks. the lookout to the falls is closed and doesn't connect with the other trail at the moment, so it is a 1 km out and back from the turn off. hilly, a good cardio workout in spots.
Whenever you see the birds flying
Second time doing this hike, great views! Waterfall, river, fields, forest…many different ‘biomes’ we walked through! Gorgeous!
The new gate system is ridiculous. Register below you get here. I didn't have signal at the gate and had to call in. It's a pain in the butt. Ontario parks is stupid

Fantastic park; varied in wooded, meadow and riverside trails. Overall very nice. Only issue is that the loop is not connected due to a portion of the trail being closed where Meadow and Dominion connect. You either have to double back or go around the barrier at your own risk.
From the parking, it's better to start towards the trail leading to the right, that way if you decide to do the whole loop, it's easier on you.

Great trail! I found that at the beginning of the trail that it was quite crowded and filled with a lot of people, but as you continued past the waterfall, the amount of people dropped off significantly, and it was much more enjoyable. The views are pretty spectacular. Make sure to stop at the look up points and when you see a path that is not on the particular trail that you’re following maybe you should go down it and see if there’s anything there because that is where you find the true beauty.
Great trail, too bad a portion near the waterfall is still closed.
Excellent trail with very nice views and some reasonably challenging climbs.
There is a section near the falls which includes the main viewing platform that is closed. Be sure to check the park alerts before you go so you know what to expect. Otherwise, a nice hike!
Fun morning hike!
Beautiful scenery!
Trail had fresh snow from the storm a couple days ago. Some areas had melted and were pretty muddy.

Hiked the Meadow Trail-Dominion Trail-Bruce Trail-Trans Canada Trail Loop.  A bit of a grind transitioning from the Dominion Trail to Bruce Trail route towards the end.  I believe it was almost a 100 Meter elevation gain on what appeared to be a 75 degree slope up this section of the trail.

Very nice trail , hiked here many times , you have to be ready for elevation and a good cardio
Make sure to book online via on reservations.ontarioparks. ca
You can book 5 days in advance and u will get the barcode for the gate .

The further I got away from the parking lot  and the area closest to the lake the better. Some people don’t know that if can carry it in full you definitely carry it out empty, but yeah once I got away from those areas it was a good walk
Super muddy and still patches of ice! Didn’t wear crampons however they could be helpful for some parts but would probably be kind of annoying in the mud!! As always a great hike!
Muddy, icy, some closed sections near  waterfall.
Very icy! Lots of fun, but be careful on the hills
Today it was a mix of slippery/slippery ice and lots of mud. But still a beautiful trail with a few water elements that makes it prettier
Make sure you pre-book online before arriving.  Icers recommended.

This trail is blocked - the view point can’t bee accessed at all. 
Conditions are great as always, but this route is impossible.
Very quiet at this time of year. Perfect if what you want is solitude.
Good trail but as the sun melted the snow on the tree branches so I did get rained on in the part  close to dominion street. But yeah I would do it again
Mill site viewing platform closed.
Leaves completely gone
Started listening to The Twilight Series on my hike. Spooky story for a spooky time of year
with Renee
Route closed off near waterfall, so had to loop back on the path at the beginning. Bruce Trail portion very nice.

This trail is lovely and not too far from the city. It’s especially beautiful in the fall but please note, you need to get a permit for parking before you arrive! You can book your time slot on the Parks Ontario Website and pay for parking there. It gets extremely busy there in the fall and if you don’t book a head then they won’t allow you in. They have put gates up at the McLaren Road parking lot.

DO NOT FORGET TO PAY FOR PARKING . Fully paved and very well maintained trail. The biodiversity along the hills is incredible, you can basically see the rapid changes in vegetation as you move up and down the hill. Some relatively hard inclines but nothing too difficult. I had no bug problems but bug spray is recommended. Most of the trail is shaded but there is about 3 km of plains. Water fall is underwhelming at best, more of a channel than anything. There are a lot of signs telling you to not go places, but someone prior already carved the way around most of these barriers.
Perfectly maintained, great signage, gorgeous fields.

Below average trail, almost no beautiful views, walking in fields or woods. Part of the trail is closed. Beware of parking scams there. They put a barcode at the entrance so you can pay, and get a ticket by email which allows you to open the entrance gate but what a surprise after you finish the trail - a parking ticket for not displaying purchased parking. How can you print a parking permit if you buy it right before the parking entrance?
Dont go when its wet or bring spikes
No bugs on a sunny Saturday morning. Only downside was that part of the trail is closed for construction but otherwise pretty and moderately challenging!

Well kept trail! Lots of biodiversity and a decent amount of elevation to challenge yourself a bit! There were some really nice benches throughout the trail to sit and enjoy the view from! The trail to the falls was unfortunately closed when we went
Trails were in excellent condition. Where are you little bugs lots of songbirds blue birds, butterflies even a turtle excellent choice for family and Abbet hikers

Kind of disappointed tbh. First half of trail was pretty buggy, not very scenic. Second part would have been great, but lots of construction. Several sections of trail were closed off…but wasn’t turning around after doing half the thing already. Had to climb under some fences and jump over some obstacles. Waterfall covered in grafatti, run down looking. Was fine for a short hike, but wouldn’t do it again. Trail was challenging at parts which was fun, some hills.
Great elevation. Water parts were the best
A beautiful walk, with lots of nice views.
Lots of climbing. Well marked. Beautiful views. Cam be some water over trails in some places if rainy. Nothing unmanageable.
Great trail but part of Dominion Trail is closed.  Take the Bruce trail to do the loop.  Must do trail!

Always great to see Credit River, rapid,clear water. It was unfortunate the view to the falls was blocked with construction, same as last year. I passed many construction area and there were many dead trees - not sure what is going on. Also picked up A LOT of garbage. People please be considerate.
Beautiful hike! Too bad there isn't a good view of the Falls. Be prepared for steep hills!
Amazing! Buggy in some areas. Part of the trail closed past the waterfall

Be prepared for some steep climbs and make sure to have shoes with good traction even on dry days. The views are lovely and it was great seeing grassland. Make sure to walk down by the river. The waterfall view wasn’t the best but we enjoyed it nonetheless.
Great trail. Bruce trail is blocked for a certain area
Well maintained trail. Good light hike. Rude woman guard at the entrance this morning. Date: 05/13/2023
Come with heavy duty boots, specially in the winter. Can get quite muddy and slippery

It was okay.  Not my favorite trail or views.  The Meadowview trail was very pretty in the snow and the Cataract/Bruce trail was a fun classic Bruce trail.

Was very disappointing to see all the deforestation going on in the middle of the park.  Didn’t look like there were cutting down just dead trees
Muddy. Some soft snow.  VERY icy on shaded areas. Do not go into those parts without crampons.

This park is always a great time and both the Bruce and the Great Trail (Trans Canada) cross through it. Good elevation changes, some decent scenery (especially Cataract Falls and the credit river). However thanks to our current melt cycle the trail conditions are mostly bad. You will either be dealing with mud pits, soft powdery snow that slips, or the ice underneath it. Particularly on the Bruce portions, which can get dicey going down. Suggest either cramp-ons or caution there. For the more adventurous: do not attempt to go down to the waterfall at the moment, as the soft snow and ice make it legit dangerous. Be content with seeing it from above or from the mill structure.

Trail was easy to moderately challenging with 250 metres of elevation gain.  Temperature was around 0 degrees celsius with crusty to packed snow.  Steep in sections, especially the Dorothy Medhurst Side Trail - micro spikes required.  Scenery was great.
Lovely but super slippery...
Super slippery today!! Bring crampons!!

It’s not that there are epic viewpoints on this trail…it’s the trail itself. You get wide trails through almost badlands type terrain, then some forest walking in the river valley, boardwalks, stairs, stone steps, and narrow paths on the sides of the river gorge. Bring traction aids as there is a lot of up and down and it could be squirrelly when icy, but it’s not super technical. Great training option to get ready for summer hiking season!
Great trail. No mud after January thaw! Excellent inclines to get the heart pumping.
Really lovely trails. A little mucky in places due to melting snow. But beautiful.
Can be a bit muddy but so beautiful! Lots of up and downs and variation in scenery!
Liked this trail even more than I thought I would! Nice variations throughout! So fun!
Great!
Lots of elevation
Very nice walk. A bit challenging. Has ups and downs and stairs. Perfect for working out.
Great trail! Route can be confusing so plan out your route before you head out
The trail start point isn't correct. Middle of the road. Need to go via the provincial park and that requires prior booking!

Did 12km today on this trail and the colours were awesome all the way through. Took lots of amazing photos. It was busy because of the long weekend and many people hiking the Bruce Trail. Highly recommend, esp if you like lots of elevation changes
Cataract Falls access is blocked. The only trees in fall colours are near the entrance.

￼ Great hike that started a little bit slow with the views but picked up near the middle in the end. It says you can’t do the waterfall loop because the trails closed but we pushed through with a slight detour and were able to complete the circle. Only do it if you didn’t wear a mask for the last two years like us.  Otherwise just do is the sign say and turned around to go back the way you came in￼￼. Having a security guard at the gate who warned you about getting a ticket if you stay too long is why this trail gets a three out of five￼
Only part of the leaves have turned red, the trail near the fall side are prettier and the other part of the trail is greener and not as outstanding when compared to other part.
Beautiful trail. Didn’t get to see the falls but the trail and scenery made up for it. It would be extra beautiful with the fall colours.
Nice trail. Lots of elevations.  Trail closed at the top - take meadow trail north to trans Canada trail.

Really nice trail! Went mid August, pathways were well maintained; however, the waterfall lookout is still closed off, making that view not the most exciting anymore. Nice mix of sun and shade, overall nice day, but I would consider this closer to easy than moderate! Took me a little under 2hrs to complete the trail.
It’s really nice average trail
Great hike. Few people. Few non shady areas. Overall great loop.
Not an easy trail but the views are worth it!

The trail head as marked here is inaccurate. anywhere within a km from it has no paring signs everywhere and pilons covering up the parking spots. you have to turn around and head back to the provicial park and pay for parking. other than that its a pretty good trail

We went to the falls lookout specifically. The terrain to get to that spot is quite challenging. A lot of ups and downs. We took lots of breaks to catch our breath. (Mind you we did this after hiking 18km the previous day) 
When you first happen upon the falls, they are quite stunning however if you continue along to the trail to the baracade, it gets more lack luster and didn't feel worth the grind to get to that point. 
Can't say this is a trail I'd repeat.
we went specifically for the falls and it was beautiful

I liked this trail very much! If you start from where AllTrails suggests, then you don't need to enter/park at the Provincial Park lot. The trail itself alternates between forest and meadow, with a fair bit of hilliness to keep it interesting. The only downside if anything is that there is no good scenic view even when you're at the elevation peak. But there is a small beach at Kettle Lake that is photo-worthy. There were also very few bugs even in the forest sections. One trail was closed, however, which required a detour from the AllTrails route.

It was alright. $7 for parking for 4 hours, which you must reserve in advance. Mix of forest and meadow. Minimal bugs, didn’t need bug spray. Fairly busy with families and dog walkers. We arrived at noon. Walked a 10km loop. The falls aren’t really worth seeing and you cannot get close to them because the trail is closed. There’s 2 sets of outhouses, which weren’t bad. Lots of hills, so a good leg workout.
Fantastic trail! Lots of ups and downs and diverse terrain. Very scenic. We got a sweat going on and not too many bugs.

The directions on here take you to a starting point where there is no parking, so you must enter the park at the main entrance and pay to park. We didn’t bother completing that tail of the trail after beginning at the entrance because it appeared to take you out the road. The rest of the trail is great! Easy to follow, with some decent inclines.
Nothing really fancy to see…path to waterfalls is closed so you can only see it from a distance.  Overall the path was easy to walk along and was very well marked, however be prepared for some hills!
Start of the trail should start from the parking lot on the east side of the park. There is no parking at the current trail beginning. Enjoyed the trail.
Good hike. if you go off the main trail near the river and take the little side Trail you can get right down to the river and there are some nice spots if you want to sit in quiet contemplation

Be warned, a reservation is needed here on the weekend. Packed up early for a 50km drive to this trail, arriving at 7:30am to learn the park does not open until 8am. No worries, a short trip to Caledon for a coffee. I arrive back at the gate at 8am, with a couple other cars lined up, but the gate locked. At 8:10 a park truck comes racing up, informs those waiting it will be a bit to get running, and proceeds to unlock the gate, proceed through, lock behind, and disappear down the road. No worries, probably something unexpected came up. About 25 mins later the attendant returns and starts talking to the first car. After a semi heated conversation the car does a  U-turn and leaves. Same for the next car. Weird. Next me, who has driven 50km, waited 45 mins beyond opening time, and am told I can't come in without a reservation done online, and I have no device to purchase such a thing. No signs, no nothing. Sad we live in a world that we have to get on the internet to check for new rules when trying to do the exact opposite, getting in nature and disconnecting. 100km round trip, and the attendant couldn't even take my contaminated COVID money, as if it was some kind of small pox blanket...even though the reservations were less than half capacity for the day, as I did check when I arrived home (I'm not usually petty like this, but I also don't often pay $30 in fuel to get a subpar coffee from McDonalds and a view of a closed park on a Saturday morning). Par for the course I suppose when the brainchild for these rules is our fine provincal government. As for the park itself, the bifold metal gates were stunning, held together firmly with a slightly rusty chain and padlock.
Lilacs were beautiful
Lots of poison ivy already growing in but very beautiful. Be mindful some parts of the trail are closed.

Wonderful park. Beautiful meadows and a few moments with the water. Popular spot. Nice variety and elevation changes in trail. Part of this loop is closed off by fences and unpassable unless you’re willing to trespass.
Great hike
Beautiful day for a hike. Trail was great. The drive INTO the location was awful, too many holes to drive through.
beautiful and well paved trail. started at bruce trail further back for parking.
1st and last 20 minutes was kind if boring but the rest was great. No mud at all and no bugs yet.
Good walk pity some of the trails were closed
The trail was very nice, a little icy but nothing overly crazy. Some of the hills were a bit rough but the views were beautiful! The waterfall was spectacular. :)
Great trail to enjoy a Sunday (or any day) winter afternoon

Excellent fun trail! As of right now the trail to the waterfall was closed but there are some ways to get around it at your own risk. Lots of elevation and would love to go again during the spring/summer and fish by the lake there!

Great winter hike!!!! We did the big loop over to the falls and back. We went clock direction. Took a side trail over to the stairway at the falls to complete the loop. If your less adventurous then you will have to hike back about 20 mins to the next short cut. There are fairly long step parts along this hike. Traction was good on hard pack trail. Suggest good hiking boots and crampons.
Started loop 2k in so add that to the overall total. Exposed escarpment at the beginning 1k in.
Great!
Great

Visited Aug 23, 2021.  It was a very hot day but I did the hike anyway.  The trail to the waterfall was closed so I trespassed.  I walked down a rocky and dangerous escarpment to see the falls and it was well worth the danger. I was soooo sweaty!!!

A very nice hike even in the drizzly rain. A bit muddy but really not bad. Part of the loop is closed so we had to hike a different route. Found an amazing spot off this trail that is a major hill but we hiked down it. Super pretty.
Some construction in areas that you really want to hike, with no notice. Overall beautiful trail.
Good Moderate trail!  Lots of options to change it up!
Lots of variation and long uphills, but the beautiful scenery made it all worthwhile
This trail is good for people who like to hike the hills and don't waste your energy to see waterfalls
Good trail and condition. One part by the waterfall is closed.
Trail is in good shape. Easy trail to hike. 50% is wide enough for an ATV.
2021-09-30:  Forks of the Credit Provincial Park & Bruce Trail
Good hike! Lots of different terrain types. Disappointed on the falls. Was expecting to get closer to the falls.
Amazing
great!

Here is some info meant to illuminate and help:
Parking lots get full quick and parking on the road outside of the gates to avoid the fee (a paltry 7.50) is a cheapo move and will get you security attention. FYI the composting washrooms have no sinks. Bring plenty of water to drink and extra to wash up with. No garbage cans, so be prepared to carry your litter.  It is a heavily trafficked area in summer/fall on weekends so there will almost always  be other people in your trail shots and (warning) NO ONE is masking up.  It is not a wide trail so you can't distance when (inevitably) passing. Plenty of dogs (leashed) and bikes (no bells but behaving well). 
Ok. Now that you are mentally prepped... The transCan trails are easy and flat, well mowed and maintained. The other trails like kettle and the falls part are moderate effort -snakey roots, mini-gullys, loose stones, inclines- and require real shoes, not flip flops. Forget kids wagons and stuff. When summer-dry, ok, if muddy would be extra slippery. The kettle lake loop is great, plenty of minnows, frogs, lilypads and fishermen. It's also short so good for little legs and time restraints.
The meadow trail is so fascinating -wildflowers and trees, snags and hills. Pollinator city, plenty of caterpillars crossing. Past the sumac stands it leads to the falls trail (washroom stop!) which is at the edge of the escarpment/bluff. Follow the falls trail and you are going dooooown. There is both poison oak and ivy in there. The shade is lovely on a hot day and we'll be back for fall colour! If you take plenty of breaks even little kids 3 yrs can do it. Remember you have to go back the same way, so uuuuup is not the best for heart conditions or joint issues. FYI at some points the only thing separating the trail from a 30 foot drop is a thin stand of trees. Breathtaking. The pocket meadows of native tufted grass and birch are also beautiful.
The falls trail stops abruptly, the end has been closed off for safety reasons. No benches.  You are not super-close to the falls, so get a good zoom on your camera. There's always someone slipping past the fence to try to get down or closer to the falls. On the way back the tiny side trails to the river are fabulous...and full of ticks. Dress appropriately.
I hope the facts above reported prepare you so you can be ready, then go and have a great time here! Totally worth it.
